import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 885

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
- [ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
- [Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
- [Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)
-/

open Nat Set Finset

namespace Erdos885

/--
For integer $n \geq 1$ we define the factor difference set of $n$ by
$D(n) = \{|a-b| : n=ab\}$.
-/
def factorDifferenceSet (n : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {d | ∃ a b : ℕ, n = a * b ∧ (d : ℤ) = |(a : ℤ) - b|}

/--
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1 < \dots < N_k$ such that
$|\cap_i D(N_i)| \geq k$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1,
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = k ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ k := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved this is true for $k=2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_2 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 2 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Jiménez-Urroz [Ji99] proved this for $k=3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_3 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 3 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Bremner [Br19] proved this for $k=4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_4 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 4 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 4 := by
  sorry

end Erdos885

reformulations.difference: The source asks for an increasing sequence N₁ < ⋯ < Nₖ; Lean instead uses a Finset of positive naturals with cardinality exactly k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Sorting such a Finset gives a strictly increasing map Fin k → ℕ with the same members and therefore the same intersection. Conversely, the image of a strictly increasing map has cardinality k. This equivalence was proved for every k in the scratch file, and consequently also covers the k=2,3,4 variants. Moreover, k≥1 makes the Finset nonempty, and each positive n has a finite factor-difference set (every difference is at most n). Thus the intersection is finite and Set.ncard agrees with ordinary cardinality.

Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdös related to common factor differences (2019), DOI 10.1142/S1793042119500581 — publisher-supplied abstract read through Crossref and https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:10.1142/S1793042119500581?fields=title,abstract,openAccessPdf; full text was inaccessible.

review.notes: Checked the definition and all four theorems. Experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully without sorry-based proofs. They establish D(0)=ℕ (excluded by every theorem), D(1)={0}, positivity of factors when n>0, finiteness of the relevant intersections, and the sequence/Finset equivalence. Concrete checks prove the k=1 and k=2 cases, with {16,100} having common differences {0,15}, and verify factor pairs for the explicit three-integer example in ErRo97. The accessible source still labels the general problem open. Although Ji99 and Br19 full texts could not be retrieved, ErRo97 supplies explicit triples and Bremner’s publisher-supplied abstract explicitly asserts four integers with four common factor differences; no mathematical claim remained unsettled.
